competency_fulfillment.rationale: Both delivery modes the competency's parenthetical names are present: an oral-style word problem at seed 44, 'Lara has 1 ribbon. A friend has 2 ribbons... how many ribbons do they have in all?', and a pictorial problem at seed 55 built from frog emoji, both posing genuine addition-in-context questions.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The 'given orally' narrative sub-case (baskets of resin, ribbons, water bottles, merchandise shirts) and the 'in pictures' sub-case (seed 55's frog-emoji row) both appear across the eight samples, matching both halves of the competency's parenthetical scope.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Seed 45 reads 'One basket has 1 water bottles. Another basket has 2 water bottles...', a singular/plural grammar mismatch, and seed 50's 'merchandise shirts' phrasing is stilted for a Grade 1 word problem, both of which could confuse an early reader even though sentence length itself stays short.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Distinct framings appear across the eight seeds: object word problems (resin at seed 42, ribbons at seed 44), a 'counting up' number-line narration (seeds 43, 46, 72), a pictorial frog-emoji model (seed 55), and an error-detection format (seed 50).

competency_alignment.rationale: Every sample, from the basket word problem at seed 42 to the frog-emoji visual at seed 55, is a genuine addition-in-context scenario ending in a question, directly matching 'solve problems... involving addition'.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Every sum produced across all eight samples is at most 3 (e.g. seed 42's 2 resin plus 1 resin, seed 55's 1 frog plus 1 more frog), so the competency's stated ceiling of sums up to 20 is never approached anywhere in this packet.
